answer: At dawn, the network starts a new epoch. It groups agents into clusters based on their behavior when they first appear. Each cluster gets paid as a single unit, which makes it costly for an attacker to create many fake agents, as they would all be treated as one entity, limiting the sybil attack's effectiveness. The network's basalt foundation of strict verification and the sable darkness of anonymous agents make it hard for attackers to hide their fake identities.
